extracted.intended_audience: NIH-funded researchers and authors (especially Northwestern Feinberg School of Medicine authors) who must comply with the NIH Public Access Policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on complying with the NIH Public Access Policy by depositing Author Accepted Manuscripts (AAMs) with zero embargo to PubMed Central (PMC), including publisher-specific permissions, deposit pathways, timing, and required metadata. Emphasis on which publishers permit immediate green OA deposit, publisher-deposit vs author self-deposit, and special instructions (e.g., stating NIH funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Green OA refers to the Author Accepted Manuscript (AAM), not the Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Green open access (OA) refers to the authors accepted manuscript, not the final, copy edited, published journal's version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under green OA, authors may deposit the AAM into an institutional or funder-specified repository (e.g., PubMed Central). Look for 'self archiving' or 'green open access' instructions on publisher sites; deposit is usually completed by the author or their delegate rather than the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-embargo green OA compatibility with NIH Public Access Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers allow deposit of the Author Accepted Manuscript into a repository with no embargo period and no fees; these policies are compatible with the NIH Public Access Policy's requirement for deposit of the AAM with no embargo to PMC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the publisher's self-archiving instructions: some require including a link to the published version of record or specific language in the uploaded manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit timing: deposit upon acceptance vs upon publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers vary on whether authors may deposit upon acceptance or only upon publication. NIH updated requirements (noted for many publishers) require AAMs for NIH-funded articles accepted on/after July 1, 2025 to be uploaded after final acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check publisher-specific language: some allow immediate deposit 'upon acceptance', some permit deposit 'upon publication', and some explicitly state deposit to NIHMS/PMC upon acceptance (e.g., ASM, ATS). Ensure you follow the correct timing for NIH-funded work and the publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility to deposit unless publisher deposits on their behalf
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are generally responsible for depositing the Author Accepted Manuscript in PMC (often via NIHMS) unless the publisher explicitly deposits on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether your journal/publisher offers to deposit (e.g., AACR will deposit AAM for corresponding authors who are AACR Active Members; BMJ deposits AAM of NIH-funded research to NIHMS upon acceptance with zero-embargo; Karger submits on authors' behalf). If publisher deposits to NIHMS rather than directly to PMC, authors may need to complete NIHMS processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: If publisher deposits for you, check deposit pathway and required author actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers deposit to NIHMS (not directly to PMC) or deposit on authors' behalf but still require author action to complete processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galter Library note: BMJ deposits to NIHMS, but authors may need to complete NIHMS steps for final deposit to PMC. Always verify whether any further steps are needed after publisher submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform the journal of NIH funding at time of submission when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals require authors to state NIH or CDC funding at time of submission (not acceptance) as a condition for permitting immediate deposit to PMC (e.g., American Academy of Pediatrics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journal instructions carefully: failing to notify funder information at submission can affect the deposit workflow and compliance. Galter Library bolded this requirement for emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include grant numbers and funding acknowledgement on manuscript/copyright forms when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers require listing NIH support, grant numbers, and contact names on the copyright form and/or title page (e.g., American Thoracic Society).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the requested funding metadata at submission/acceptance to facilitate compliance and deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: When posting AAM, include a link and citation to the Version of Record when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers require that the AAM be posted with a hyperlink to the Final Published Version on the publisher's website and an explanatory citation note (e.g., AAAS/Science guidance: include a hyperlink and note: 'This is the author's version... definitive version was published in [Title] on [date]; DOI: [insert DOI number].').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact citation and the recommended explanatory language if the publisher provides it to avoid violating terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark deposited AAM as not the Version of Record and provide attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When archiving your Author Accepted Manuscript, make clear that it is not the final Version of Record and include attribution and a link to the Version of Record (e.g., Portland Press guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wording such as 'this is the author's accepted manuscript' and include citation details and DOI/URL to the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing requirements vary (CC BY, CC BY-NC-ND, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agreements allow or require particular licenses for deposited material (e.g., ACS 'read and green' agreement allows deposit with no embargo and a Creative Commons license of choice (CC BY or CC BY-NC-ND) for hybrid journals). ASM permits posting under a CC-BY license if certain linking/credit conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the publisher's policy for license requirements or options and whether opting into a program (e.g., CARLI/ACS) requires selecting a particular publishing agreement option to retain rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gold Open Access publication usually means publisher will deposit the Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article is published Gold OA, the publisher often deposits the Version of Record (VoR) to PMC on the official date of publication, ensuring public availability without embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing Gold OA, verify whether the publisher will deposit to PMC on your behalf; if so, no author deposit action may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher-specific fees or charges for green route may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers or journals charge fees for choosing the green route or for certain deposit/archiving options (e.g., Journal of Cell Biology and Journal of Experimental Medicine charge a $2,000 page fee for the green route under Rockefeller University Press).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check publisher/journal-specific terms and fee schedules before choosing green OA options; there may be alternatives or waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers may automatically deposit AAM for NIH-funded authors for some journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers have arranged automatic PMC deposit of the AAM for articles that indicate NIH funding at submission or acceptance, meaning authors do not need to deposit via NIHMS (e.g., some Sage journals, ASM primary research journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult publisher funder compliance pages or journal lists to see whether your journal participates in automatic deposit programs and whether any author action is still required.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a journal cannot deposit or is not indexed, authors remain responsible for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain journal types or sections (e.g., ASHA 'Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups') may not be indexed by PubMed and the publisher cannot process deposit; NIH-funded authors must deposit the accepted manuscript to PMC themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the publisher cannot deposit, go directly to the NIH Manuscript Submission system (NIHMS) to deposit and comply with NIH public access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher policies differ by journal — check journal- and publisher-level policies and CTAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some publishers have mixed policies across journals (e.g., Cambridge University Press: some journals allow immediate deposit, others have embargoes). Copyright Transfer Agreements (CTAs) and exclusive licenses may contain different terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the specific journal's author instructions, copyright/licensing agreements, and any sample license language provided by the publisher to determine your rights and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional or consortial agreements can change author rights/options
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements between institutions/consortia and publishers (e.g., CARLI and ACS 'read and green' agreement effective January 2026) can grant participating authors rights to deposit AAMs with no embargo if authors opt-in during the Journal Publishing Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your institution is party to such agreements, follow the opt-in steps on the publisher's Journal Publishing Agreement to retain the necessary rights; there may be no fee for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of acceptable repositories and non-commercial repository restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers like ACM define where authors may post accepted versions (author homepage, institutional repository, any repository legally mandated by funder, non-commercial repositories that do not duplicate ACM tables of contents). Non-commercial repositories are defined as non-profit organizations that do not charge for access or profit from serving scholarly articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the repository you use complies with the publisher's allowed-list and include the recommended citation/attribution statement when posting submitted or accepted versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers may offer waivers or exceptional support to meet funder mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: For journals with embargoes or APCs, some publishers (e.g., Cambridge University Press) may provide exceptional waivers of fees or other support to help authors comply with funder policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the publisher or check policy pages to request waivers/exceptions if APCs would prevent compliance with NIH mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping and metadata: include required metadata to support PMC deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits often require metadata such as full citation, DOI, grant number, and funding statements; some publishers supply accepted manuscript files and metadata to support author submissions (e.g., Annual Reviews will provide the accepted manuscript, metadata, and DOI to support author submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep accurate records and ensure the deposit includes required metadata so NIHMS/PMC processing can complete successfully.
